key_insight: Training biomedical QA models on their own generated answers caused bigger performance drops over generations than retraining on original human data, especially for the larger model.
clinical_relevance: Recursive synthetic-data training may degrade answer quality and entity accuracy in biomedical QA, so human-curated data remain important for safer model maintenance.
method: Compared recursive synthetic-data training vs a human-control loop in PubMedQA.
Tested Qwen2.5 models at 0.5B and 3B parameters across four generations (G0–G3).
Evaluated disease/chemical entity F1, context support, lexical/semantic similarity, answer length, and repetition.
evidence_signal: Across two seeds and a 1,000-sample expert-labeled evaluation set, the recursive condition showed larger declines in disease F1, chemical F1, context-supported rate, ROUGE-L, and cosine similarity than the human-control condition.
watch_item: These results show degradation in benchmark QA metrics, but they do not prove clinical hallucination rates or imply universal model collapse in real-world use.
paper_title: Recursive LLM Degradation in Biomedical Question Answering: A Cross-Generation Study
